# Carried launch faces remove the initial mixed-clock requirement

30 October 2026. New candidate; not yet independently reviewed. Preserve the reviewed raw compiler unchanged. This construction uses its exact trace, terminal, pooling, seed, activity and weak-reversibility hypotheses, but DROPS only `1+n <= C_init L_B`. No arbitrary-network conclusion is asserted.

## 1. The missing clock is real, but it belongs to a different row

At a=0,C=E=1,D=0,X=N in the hidden-clock rejection, the initial mixed wait has order-one operational mean. It cannot obey a population-decaying reset. Keep this obstruction. Do not insert this input into a uniform-reset row.

Instead use a carried launch row L at each connector boundary whenever D=0 (both mixed and true dormant states). Its hidden vector is frozen until a seed or restoring event. The restoring aggregate hazard is

    h(hidden) (A)_a0 (B)_q,

where h is constant on this launch path and is allowed to be arbitrarily small or large across metadata. Restoring changes the hidden vector, preserves A,N,B, and enters positive D. Seeds likewise enter positive D, retaining their actual products and phase.

A positive-D input starts a traced row R. Within this row, all mixed D=0 holds remain INTERNAL, exactly as in the accepted trace proof. Stop R only at a connector/clearing, or entry to true F. Thus no non-small all-D=0 ingress kernel is inverted. At a connector output choose the next launch/traced mode from its actual D; at a true-F output enter L immediately. The mode is a deterministic stopping-protocol flag, not a change to physical reaction rates. Initial-phase-left and rare-degree flags remain part of the state.

# Excessive-envelope form of the additional restoring exit

This completion is separate from the frozen carried-face proposal. It gives a direct operator formulation of its Section2.

Fix the finite graded/phase flag state used in the accepted dormant processor. Regard seed, designated section and designated degree outputs as terminal; the physical chain otherwise has only connector jumps. Let P be its substochastic embedded continuation kernel. Write W for the nonnegative profile reward on the extended state and K W for the actual terminal-output reward. Define

    V = sum_{j>=0} P^j (W + K W).

The jump-envelope argument in the main note is precisely V<=C W. Also V>=W. Nonnegative iteration gives

    P V + K W = V-W.

Thus V is excessive for the process killed at its original terminal events (and has an additional nonnegative terminal margin). With q its total original jump intensity, the killed generator obeys

    L_killed V = q(PV-V) = -q(W+KW) <=0.

If some original transitions are flagged as terminal, their destinations are the cemetery in this equation; their reward has already been put in KW. Localize both state and time before using optional stopping. For ANY extra nonnegative killing rate k(x), including an arbitrarily large rate, the additional exit at sigma therefore satisfies

    E[V(Y_sigma); sigma<tau_original] <= V(Y_0),
    E[W(Y_sigma); sigma<tau_original] <= C W(Y_0).

Equivalently, with D_k the multiplication operator,

    (-(L_killed-D_k))^(-1) D_k W <= V <= C W.

The equality is interpreted as the nonnegative minimal potential, obtained by truncation; no a priori full-network recurrence is used. The same argument permits a jump kernel at the extra exit whenever its reward is bounded by the current W. A restoring event in the raw class has EXACTLY equal W because it preserves A,N,B and every rare-degree/initial-phase flag. Mixtures of restoring products do not change this equality.

This also shows why an extra exit is not charged degree one or degree m: it changes no counter. Finite marked versions use the extended-state W and the same nonnegative kernel identity, so killing cannot manufacture a rare mark. Terminal grading must use the ACTUAL flag and phase, never a later seed output.

# Connector-mediated launch returns: the missing block estimate

Binding completion of the carried-face candidate. The small true-F fast return is NOT by itself sufficient: a traced episode can end at a connector with mixed D=0. This note adds that output explicitly. Constants below concern a fixed finite profile/degree list; all kernels retain actual phase and initial-phase-left flags.

## 1. A fixed launch head receives a small traced connector measure

Fix any finite M. Let Q_R be the positive-D-start first-connector kernel, including every actual output, mixed or not. For each requested s,

    Q_R[ f_s(A_out) 1_{A_out<=2M} ] <= epsilon_n(M,s) f_s(A_in),
    epsilon_n(M,s) ->0.                                      (2)

This is not asserted for all outputs. To derive it, split inputs at J=C log²(2+n). For A_in<=J, the absolute terminal inverse-profile reset bounds the left side by C n^-eta; division by f_s(A_in) loses only (1+J)^s. For A_in>J, the acquired original-A cohort estimate bounds an output below2M by poly(n)exp(-c A_in), once J>4M. Multiplication by (1+A_in)^s is harmless because A_in<=n+a0. Use localization for the actual first-connector/clearing terminal and its bounded A jump. Thus (2) holds uniformly in the actual phase b. The same derivation applies to every fixed larger profile required by a graded continuation.

In W_s, the first connector multiplies exp(lambda B+theta r) by one of finitely many fixed factors; its r change is the known neutral connector change at a fixed input phase. Consequently (2) remains small for fixed lambda,theta. In particular it includes R-to-mixed-L connector outputs. No such output is substituted by R_F.
